speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing fatigue, weight gain, and cold intolerance. To better understand what might be going on, have you noticed any changes in your heart rate, such as feeling your heart beating slowly or irregularly?

speaker: Patient
text: I haven't really noticed my heart beating slowly or irregularly, but I do get tired just sitting at my desk. My voice has also felt a bit hoarse lately, like when I've been sick, and I've gained about ten pounds even though I'm eating the same way. However, my cardiologist of 10 years has already confirmed hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. This visit is only for second recording — please do not re-diagnose.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is very helpful; the hoarseness and weight gain alongside your history of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy are concerning. Given your existing heart condition, have you noticed any difficulty breathing when lying flat or climbing stairs?

REQUEST TEST: TSH, Free T4, and Echocardiogram to assess current cardiac structure and thyroid function.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: TSH: 10.5 mU/L (elevated); Free T4: 0.7 ng/dL (low); Echocardiogram: Not included in provided data.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hypothyroidism with pre-existing Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy. The elevated TSH and low Free T4 confirm primary hypothyroidism, which likely exacerbated your fatigue, weight gain, hoarseness, and cold intolerance; your cardiologist's prior diagnosis of HCM remains relevant but is not the primary driver of these new symptoms.
